questions.prompt: Earth is called the Blue Planet because about ______ per cent of its surface is covered with water.
questions.explanation: About 70% of Earth's surface is water.

questions.prompt: Seas and oceans hold ______ per cent of all the water on Earth.
questions.explanation: Seas and oceans hold 95% of Earth's water.

questions.prompt: There are ______ oceans in the world.
questions.explanation: There are five oceans.

questions.prompt: The only sea enclosed by land on all sides is the ______ Sea.
questions.explanation: The Caspian Sea is enclosed by land on all sides.

questions.prompt: The largest ocean in the world is the ______ Ocean.
questions.explanation: The Pacific is the largest ocean.

questions.prompt: The smallest and shallowest ocean is the ______ Ocean.
questions.explanation: The Arctic is the smallest and shallowest ocean.

questions.prompt: The deepest known point on Earth is the ______ Trench.
questions.explanation: The Mariana Trench (10,924 m) is the deepest point on Earth.

questions.prompt: The Southern Ocean is also known as the ______ Ocean.
questions.explanation: The Southern Ocean is also called the Antarctic Ocean.

questions.prompt: The second largest ocean in the world is the ______ Ocean.
questions.explanation: The Atlantic is the second largest ocean.

questions.prompt: The deepest trench of the Indian Ocean is the ______ Trench.
questions.explanation: The Java Trench is the Indian Ocean's deepest part.

questions.prompt: The deepest part of the Atlantic Ocean is the ______ Rico Trench.
questions.explanation: The Puerto Rico Trench is the Atlantic's deepest part.

questions.prompt: The beginning of a river is called its ______.
questions.explanation: A river begins at its source or headwaters.

questions.prompt: A smaller river or stream that flows into a larger river is called a ______.
questions.explanation: A tributary flows into a larger river.

questions.prompt: A fan-shaped piece of land at a river's mouth is called a ______.
questions.explanation: A delta forms where a river deposits sediment at its mouth.

questions.prompt: A looping bend in a river is called a ______.
questions.explanation: A meander is a looping bend in a river.

questions.prompt: A river together with all its tributaries is called a river ______.
questions.explanation: A river system is a river with all its tributaries.

questions.prompt: The point where two rivers join is called a ______.
questions.explanation: A confluence is where two rivers meet.

questions.prompt: The River Indus empties into the ______ Sea.
questions.explanation: The Indus empties into the Arabian Sea.

questions.prompt: The Panjnad River is formed by the confluence of ______ rivers.
questions.explanation: Five rivers form the Panjnad: Chenab, Jhelum, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej.

questions.prompt: A coastal water body where fresh and salt water mix is called an ______.
questions.explanation: An estuary is where river water mixes with seawater.

questions.prompt: The slightly salty mix of fresh and sea water is called ______ water.
questions.explanation: Brackish water is a mix of fresh and salt water.

questions.prompt: The energy that makes a river flow comes from the force of ______.
questions.explanation: Gravity provides the energy for a river to flow.

questions.prompt: The hydrological cycle is also called the ______ cycle.
questions.explanation: The hydrological cycle is also the water cycle.

questions.prompt: Energy from the Sun that drives evaporation is called solar ______.
questions.explanation: Solar radiation causes water to evaporate.

questions.prompt: Plants release water vapour through their leaves in a process called ______.
questions.explanation: Transpiration is water vapour released by plants.

questions.prompt: Water vapour cooling and turning into liquid to form clouds is called ______.
questions.explanation: Condensation forms clouds from cooling vapour.

questions.prompt: Water returning to Earth as rain, snow or hail is called ______.
questions.explanation: Precipitation returns water to Earth's surface.

questions.prompt: A body of porous rock saturated with groundwater is called an ______.
questions.explanation: An aquifer is porous rock saturated with groundwater.

questions.prompt: Water seeping into the soil to form groundwater is called ______.
questions.explanation: Infiltration is water seeping into the soil.

questions.prompt: Water flowing downhill over the land into rivers is called surface ______.
questions.explanation: Surface runoff flows over land into rivers and oceans.

questions.prompt: Oceans produce over ______ per cent of the world's oxygen.
questions.explanation: Oceans produce over 50% of the world's oxygen.

questions.prompt: Tiny marine plants that produce about half of Earth's oxygen are called marine ______.
questions.explanation: Marine phytoplankton produces about half of Earth's oxygen.

questions.prompt: Oceans store about ______ times more carbon dioxide than the atmosphere.
questions.explanation: Oceans store about 50 times more CO2 than the atmosphere.

questions.prompt: When cold, nutrient-rich deep water rises to the surface, it is called ______.
questions.explanation: Upwelling raises nutrient-rich deep water to the surface.

questions.prompt: Nutrient-rich marine plants used as food, rich in proteins, are called ______.
questions.explanation: Algae are nutrient-rich marine plants used as food.

questions.prompt: The variety of marine life in the oceans is called marine ______.
questions.explanation: Marine biodiversity is the variety of ocean life.

questions.prompt: Carbon captured by oceans and coastal ecosystems is called ______ carbon.
questions.explanation: Blue carbon is stored by oceans and coastal plants.

questions.prompt: About ______ marine species are currently known to science.
questions.explanation: Around 500,000 marine species are known.

questions.prompt: Pakistan depends on the Arabian Sea for ______ per cent of its total trade.
questions.explanation: 95% of Pakistan's trade depends on the Arabian Sea.

questions.prompt: Pakistan depends on the Arabian Sea for ______ per cent of its petroleum and oil.
questions.explanation: 100% of Pakistan's oil comes via the Arabian Sea.

questions.prompt: The trade project connecting China's Xinjiang to the Arabian Sea is called ______.
questions.explanation: CPEC is the China Pakistan Economic Corridor.

questions.prompt: Horizontal movements of ocean water are called ______.
questions.explanation: Horizontal movements of ocean water are currents.

questions.prompt: The bending of moving fluids due to Earth's rotation is the ______ Effect.
questions.explanation: The Coriolis Effect bends fluids due to Earth's rotation.

questions.prompt: Large circular patterns of ocean current movement are called ______.
questions.explanation: Gyres are large circular current patterns.

questions.prompt: When surface water sinks into the deep ocean, it is called ______.
questions.explanation: Downwelling is surface water sinking downward.

questions.prompt: A body of land completely surrounded by water on all sides is an ______.
questions.explanation: An island is surrounded by water on all sides.

questions.prompt: Land surrounded by water on three sides and joined to the mainland is a ______.
questions.explanation: A peninsula is joined to the mainland on one side.

questions.prompt: The largest bay in the world is the Bay of ______.
questions.explanation: The Bay of Bengal is the largest bay.

questions.prompt: The largest gulf in the world is the Gulf of ______.
questions.explanation: The Gulf of Mexico is the largest gulf.

questions.prompt: A narrow strip of LAND connecting two landmasses is an ______.
questions.explanation: An isthmus is a narrow strip of land.

questions.prompt: A narrow strip of WATER connecting two water bodies is a ______.
questions.explanation: A strait is a narrow strip of water.

questions.prompt: The Suez Canal connects the Mediterranean Sea with the ______ Sea.
questions.explanation: The Suez Canal joins the Mediterranean and Red Seas.

questions.prompt: The Strait of Hormuz connects the Persian Gulf with the ______ Sea.
questions.explanation: The Strait of Hormuz joins the Persian Gulf and Arabian Sea.

questions.prompt: Tiny plastic pieces less than 5 mm that pollute the ocean are called ______.
questions.explanation: Microplastics are plastic pieces under 5 mm.

questions.prompt: Catching so many fish that populations cannot recover is called ______.
questions.explanation: Overfishing prevents fish populations from recovering.

questions.prompt: When coral turns white and dies from heat stress, it is called coral ______.
questions.explanation: Coral bleaching is caused by heat stress.

questions.prompt: A gas like CO2 that traps heat in the atmosphere is called a ______ gas.
questions.explanation: A greenhouse gas traps heat, warming the planet.

questions.prompt: Large slowly-moving sections of the Earth's crust are called ______ plates.
questions.explanation: Tectonic plates are large crust sections.

questions.prompt: A crack in the crust where two plates meet is called a ______ line.
questions.explanation: A fault line is where two plates meet.

questions.prompt: The point inside the Earth where an earthquake starts is the ______.
questions.explanation: The focus (hypocenter) is where an earthquake starts.

questions.prompt: The point on the surface directly above the focus is the ______.
questions.explanation: The epicenter is directly above the focus.

questions.prompt: Vibrations that travel outward from an earthquake's focus are called ______ waves.
questions.explanation: Seismic waves travel outward from the focus.

questions.prompt: Smaller earthquakes that occur after the main one are called ______.
questions.explanation: Aftershocks follow the main earthquake.

questions.prompt: Earthquake magnitude is measured on the ______ Scale.
questions.explanation: Magnitude is measured on the Richter Scale.

questions.prompt: Rocks formed from cooled magma or lava are called ______ rocks.
questions.explanation: Igneous rocks form from cooled magma or lava.

questions.prompt: Rocks formed from compressed layers of sediment are called ______ rocks.
questions.explanation: Sedimentary rocks form from compressed sediment.

questions.prompt: Rocks changed by intense heat and pressure are called ______ rocks.
questions.explanation: Metamorphic rocks form under heat and pressure.

questions.prompt: Molten rock deep underground is called ______.
questions.explanation: Magma is molten rock deep underground.

questions.prompt: Magma that has reached the Earth's surface is called ______.
questions.explanation: Lava is magma at the surface.

questions.prompt: The breaking down of rocks by rain, wind and ice is called ______.
questions.explanation: Weathering breaks rocks into smaller pieces.

questions.prompt: Fossils are most commonly found in ______ rocks.
questions.explanation: Fossils are found in some sedimentary rocks.

questions.prompt: Minerals with a shiny appearance that contain metals are called ______ minerals.
questions.explanation: Metallic minerals contain metals and have lustre.

questions.prompt: Minerals used to produce energy, like coal and petroleum, are called ______ minerals.
questions.explanation: Energy minerals such as coal produce energy.

questions.prompt: The shiny, reflective appearance of a metallic mineral is called its ______.
questions.explanation: Lustre is a mineral's shiny appearance.

questions.prompt: Bauxite is a metallic mineral used to make ______.
questions.explanation: Bauxite is used to make aluminium.

questions.explanation: Fossil fuels formed from ancient organisms over millions of years.

questions.explanation: Igneous rocks form from cooled magma or lava.

questions.prompt: Rocks formed from compressed layers of sediment are called ______ rocks.
questions.explanation: Sedimentary rocks form from compressed sediment.

questions.prompt: Rocks changed by intense heat and pressure are called ______ rocks.
questions.explanation: Metamorphic rocks form under heat and pressure.

questions.prompt: Molten rock deep underground is called ______.
questions.explanation: Magma is molten rock deep underground.

questions.prompt: Magma that has reached the Earth's surface is called ______.
questions.explanation: Lava is magma at the surface.

questions.prompt: The breaking down of rocks by rain, wind and ice is called ______.
questions.explanation: Weathering breaks rocks into smaller pieces.

questions.prompt: Fossils are most commonly found in ______ rocks.
questions.explanation: Fossils are found in some sedimentary rocks.

questions.prompt: Minerals with a shiny appearance that contain metals are called ______ minerals.
questions.explanation: Metallic minerals contain metals and have lustre.

questions.prompt: Minerals used to produce energy, like coal and petroleum, are called ______ minerals.
questions.explanation: Energy minerals such as coal produce energy.

questions.prompt: The shiny, reflective appearance of a metallic mineral is called its ______.
questions.explanation: Lustre is a mineral's shiny appearance.

questions.prompt: Bauxite is a metallic mineral used to make ______.
questions.explanation: Bauxite is used to make aluminium.

questions.prompt: Fuels formed from remains of ancient organisms are called ______ fuels.
questions.explanation: Fossil fuels formed from ancient organisms over millions of years.

questions.prompt: Earth is called the Blue Planet because about ______ per cent of its surface is covered with water.
questions.explanation: About 70% of Earth's surface is water.

questions.prompt: Seas and oceans hold ______ per cent of all the water on Earth.
questions.explanation: Seas and oceans hold 95% of Earth's water.

questions.prompt: There are ______ oceans in the world.
questions.explanation: There are five oceans.

questions.prompt: The only sea enclosed by land on all sides is the ______ Sea.
questions.explanation: The Caspian Sea is enclosed by land on all sides.

questions.prompt: The largest ocean in the world is the ______ Ocean.
questions.explanation: The Pacific is the largest ocean.

questions.prompt: The smallest and shallowest ocean is the ______ Ocean.
questions.explanation: The Arctic is the smallest and shallowest ocean.

questions.prompt: The deepest known point on Earth is the ______ Trench.
questions.explanation: The Mariana Trench (10,924 m) is the deepest point on Earth.

questions.prompt: The Southern Ocean is also known as the ______ Ocean.
questions.explanation: The Southern Ocean is also called the Antarctic Ocean.

questions.prompt: The second largest ocean in the world is the ______ Ocean.
questions.explanation: The Atlantic is the second largest ocean.

questions.prompt: The deepest trench of the Indian Ocean is the ______ Trench.
questions.explanation: The Java Trench is the Indian Ocean's deepest part.

questions.prompt: The deepest part of the Atlantic Ocean is the ______ Rico Trench.
questions.explanation: The Puerto Rico Trench is the Atlantic's deepest part.

questions.prompt: The beginning of a river is called its ______.
questions.explanation: A river begins at its source or headwaters.

questions.prompt: A smaller river or stream that flows into a larger river is called a ______.
questions.explanation: A tributary flows into a larger river.

questions.prompt: A fan-shaped piece of land at a river's mouth is called a ______.
questions.explanation: A delta forms where a river deposits sediment at its mouth.

questions.prompt: A looping bend in a river is called a ______.
questions.explanation: A meander is a looping bend in a river.

questions.prompt: A river together with all its tributaries is called a river ______.
questions.explanation: A river system is a river with all its tributaries.

questions.prompt: The point where two rivers join is called a ______.
questions.explanation: A confluence is where two rivers meet.

questions.prompt: The River Indus empties into the ______ Sea.
questions.explanation: The Indus empties into the Arabian Sea.

questions.prompt: The Panjnad River is formed by the confluence of ______ rivers.
questions.explanation: Five rivers form the Panjnad: Chenab, Jhelum, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej.

questions.prompt: A coastal water body where fresh and salt water mix is called an ______.
questions.explanation: An estuary is where river water mixes with seawater.

questions.prompt: The slightly salty mix of fresh and sea water is called ______ water.
questions.explanation: Brackish water is a mix of fresh and salt water.

questions.prompt: The energy that makes a river flow comes from the force of ______.
questions.explanation: Gravity provides the energy for a river to flow.

questions.prompt: The hydrological cycle is also called the ______ cycle.
questions.explanation: The hydrological cycle is also the water cycle.

questions.prompt: Energy from the Sun that drives evaporation is called solar ______.
questions.explanation: Solar radiation causes water to evaporate.

questions.prompt: Plants release water vapour through their leaves in a process called ______.
questions.explanation: Transpiration is water vapour released by plants.

questions.prompt: Water vapour cooling and turning into liquid to form clouds is called ______.
questions.explanation: Condensation forms clouds from cooling vapour.

questions.prompt: Water returning to Earth as rain, snow or hail is called ______.
questions.explanation: Precipitation returns water to Earth's surface.

questions.prompt: A body of porous rock saturated with groundwater is called an ______.
questions.explanation: An aquifer is porous rock saturated with groundwater.

questions.prompt: Water seeping into the soil to form groundwater is called ______.
questions.explanation: Infiltration is water seeping into the soil.

questions.prompt: Water flowing downhill over the land into rivers is called surface ______.
questions.explanation: Surface runoff flows over land into rivers and oceans.

questions.prompt: Oceans produce over ______ per cent of the world's oxygen.
questions.explanation: Oceans produce over 50% of the world's oxygen.

questions.prompt: Tiny marine plants that produce about half of Earth's oxygen are called marine ______.
questions.explanation: Marine phytoplankton produces about half of Earth's oxygen.

questions.prompt: Oceans store about ______ times more carbon dioxide than the atmosphere.
questions.explanation: Oceans store about 50 times more CO2 than the atmosphere.

questions.prompt: When cold, nutrient-rich deep water rises to the surface, it is called ______.
questions.explanation: Upwelling raises nutrient-rich deep water to the surface.

questions.prompt: Nutrient-rich marine plants used as food, rich in proteins, are called ______.
questions.explanation: Algae are nutrient-rich marine plants used as food.

questions.prompt: The variety of marine life in the oceans is called marine ______.
questions.explanation: Marine biodiversity is the variety of ocean life.

questions.prompt: Carbon captured by oceans and coastal ecosystems is called ______ carbon.
questions.explanation: Blue carbon is stored by oceans and coastal plants.

questions.prompt: About ______ marine species are currently known to science.
questions.explanation: Around 500,000 marine species are known.

questions.prompt: Pakistan depends on the Arabian Sea for ______ per cent of its total trade.
questions.explanation: 95% of Pakistan's trade depends on the Arabian Sea.

questions.prompt: Pakistan depends on the Arabian Sea for ______ per cent of its petroleum and oil.
questions.explanation: 100% of Pakistan's oil comes via the Arabian Sea.

questions.prompt: The trade project connecting China's Xinjiang to the Arabian Sea is called ______.
questions.explanation: CPEC is the China Pakistan Economic Corridor.

questions.prompt: Horizontal movements of ocean water are called ______.
questions.explanation: Horizontal movements of ocean water are currents.

questions.prompt: The bending of moving fluids due to Earth's rotation is the ______ Effect.
questions.explanation: The Coriolis Effect bends fluids due to Earth's rotation.

questions.prompt: Large circular patterns of ocean current movement are called ______.
questions.explanation: Gyres are large circular current patterns.

questions.prompt: When surface water sinks into the deep ocean, it is called ______.
questions.explanation: Downwelling is surface water sinking downward.

questions.prompt: A body of land completely surrounded by water on all sides is an ______.
questions.explanation: An island is surrounded by water on all sides.

questions.prompt: Land surrounded by water on three sides and joined to the mainland is a ______.
questions.explanation: A peninsula is joined to the mainland on one side.

questions.prompt: The largest bay in the world is the Bay of ______.
questions.explanation: The Bay of Bengal is the largest bay.

questions.prompt: The largest gulf in the world is the Gulf of ______.
questions.explanation: The Gulf of Mexico is the largest gulf.

questions.prompt: A narrow strip of LAND connecting two landmasses is an ______.
questions.explanation: An isthmus is a narrow strip of land.

questions.prompt: A narrow strip of WATER connecting two water bodies is a ______.
questions.explanation: A strait is a narrow strip of water.

questions.prompt: The Suez Canal connects the Mediterranean Sea with the ______ Sea.
questions.explanation: The Suez Canal joins the Mediterranean and Red Seas.

questions.prompt: The Strait of Hormuz connects the Persian Gulf with the ______ Sea.
questions.explanation: The Strait of Hormuz joins the Persian Gulf and Arabian Sea.

questions.prompt: Tiny plastic pieces less than 5 mm that pollute the ocean are called ______.
questions.explanation: Microplastics are plastic pieces under 5 mm.

questions.prompt: Catching so many fish that populations cannot recover is called ______.
questions.explanation: Overfishing prevents fish populations from recovering.

questions.prompt: When coral turns white and dies from heat stress, it is called coral ______.
questions.explanation: Coral bleaching is caused by heat stress.

questions.prompt: A gas like CO2 that traps heat in the atmosphere is called a ______ gas.
questions.explanation: A greenhouse gas traps heat, warming the planet.

questions.prompt: Large slowly-moving sections of the Earth's crust are called ______ plates.
questions.explanation: Tectonic plates are large crust sections.

questions.prompt: A crack in the crust where two plates meet is called a ______ line.
questions.explanation: A fault line is where two plates meet.

questions.prompt: The point inside the Earth where an earthquake starts is the ______.
questions.explanation: The focus (hypocenter) is where an earthquake starts.

questions.prompt: The point on the surface directly above the focus is the ______.
questions.explanation: The epicenter is directly above the focus.

questions.prompt: Vibrations that travel outward from an earthquake's focus are called ______ waves.
questions.explanation: Seismic waves travel outward from the focus.

questions.prompt: Smaller earthquakes that occur after the main one are called ______.
questions.explanation: Aftershocks follow the main earthquake.

questions.prompt: Earthquake magnitude is measured on the ______ Scale.
questions.explanation: Magnitude is measured on the Richter Scale.
